doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: 'God's love made visible' in the cantata
summary: Story of Iola telling Dave in a Volkswagen bus that his Christmas cantata lacked 'God's love made visible', and the lyric they wrote on the drive to Vermont.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I want to ask you about, I thought this was just a wonderful little story, that Dave told me that you were driving in a Volkswagen bus up to a camp where your son was and he was trying to finish one of his cantatas, and he said, “Iola I’ve finished.” And you were driving and you said, “No you haven’t.” He said, “Why?” And you said, “Because you’ve left out the most important thing about Christmas, and that is God’s love made visible.” And he said, “I can’t fit that in here.” And you replied, “Well fine, just see what you can do.” I think that’s such a great exchange.
Yeah, that’s true. And the rest of the way to Vermont we were making up words that would go with that five-four rhythm — I said, “See it’s easy.” God’s love made visible/He is invincible.
What a great little scene, in the back of the van. And then didn’t he finish it in the attic or something?
Yeah. And that is the most popular section of that cantata, as a piece by itself, it’s sung a lot. In fact it’s in some hymn books.
